card.title: Hand Over the Proof
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the actual note, not your description.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want the words that don't get your emphasis.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me the one line you're using to decide for me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands the note; A3 rejects mediated emphasis and A5 narrows access to the line being used to decide for A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 reading aloud prompts A3 objection to interpretation; B4 privacy prompts A5 a limited line rather than the whole note.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers partial disclosure and B4 protects privacy, forcing a credible access negotiation.

heightening.evidence: B4 objection produces a narrower, more justified demand; the development is clear but modest.

specificity.evidence: A1 actual note and A5 a decision affecting A are playable, but the decision itself stays generic.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 words without your emphasis and A5 one line keep the dispute concise and specific to information access.
